transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I don’t want to sound like I’m making a big fuss, doctor. I try to keep things together. But I came in because people keep acting like I’m just imagining it, and I don’t think I am.

It feels like the hospital people, and some people from the agency, have been watching our house… and even my cleaning routes. Like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband. I know that might sound strange, but that’s what’s been going on.
Do you feel that people are watching you or monitoring your actions even when there's no evidence that they are?

I… yes, I do feel that way. I know there isn’t anything I can point to that would prove it, and I’m not trying to make trouble or sound paranoid or anything.

But it really feels like the hospital people, and some folks from the agency, have been keeping an eye on our house… and even where I go on my cleaning routes. Like they’re checking up on whether I’m taking proper care of my husband. I can’t shake that feeling.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others don’t seem to notice, like voices or presences, even when you’re alone?

I… I don’t want you to think I’m strange. It’s not all the time. But sometimes, even when the house is quiet, I hear a woman’s voice near the kitchen window. It’s clear, like she’s right there standing outside or just by it.

She’ll say things like I should check the locks, or move his pills. I usually try to just… do what makes sense and not make a big deal of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had any medical conditions or been on any medications that might explain these experiences with the voices or feelings of being watched?

I’m not really sure, doctor. I don’t know of any medical condition that would explain it… at least nobody’s told me that. And I’m not trying to blame medicine or anything.

I haven’t noticed it being tied to anything like that, but maybe there’s something I wouldn’t know to look for. What kind of medications or conditions do you mean?

Do these experiences with the voices or feeling watched happen mostly when you’re feeling particularly down, anxious, or in a very low or very high mood, or do they happen even when your mood feels about normal?

I think… it’s not only when my mood is really up or really down. I mean, it might feel worse when I’m anxious, maybe, but there was a quieter stretch for a few weeks where I was sleeping more and not rushing around so much.

Even then, I still heard that woman’s voice by the kitchen window sometimes, and I still had the feeling the agency was watching us. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right, but it didn’t completely go away just because I was calmer.
Are there times when you experience the voices or the feeling of being watched even when your mood feels completely normal and not anxious, down, or elevated at all?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there was a quieter spell for a few weeks where I wasn’t so worked up. I was sleeping more, not rushing around as much, and I felt more… normal, I guess.

But even then, I still heard the woman’s voice by the kitchen window sometimes. And I still felt like the agency was watching us. So it wasn’t only when I was anxious or in a bad mood. Is that what you mean?
Even though others say there's no reason to believe you're being watched or that there's someone by the window, do you still feel certain that these things are really happening?

I know people say there’s no reason, and I don’t want to sound difficult… but yes, I do still feel pretty sure it’s happening.

That’s kind of why I’m here, because everyone keeps acting like I’m just imagining it. But I know the hospital people, and some people from the agency, have been watching our house and my cleaning routes. I think they’re checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. I’m not trying to make trouble by saying that… it just feels real to me.
Do you believe that the people watching you or the voice you hear have a specific purpose or plan related to you, like trying to test you, control you, or make sure you’re doing things right?

Yes… I mean, I don’t think they’re trying to hurt me exactly. I hope not. But it does feel like there’s a purpose to it.

Like they’re watching the house and my cleaning routes to see if I’m doing things right, especially with taking care of my husband. The hospital people, and maybe people from the agency… it feels like they’re checking up on me.

I know that probably sounds strange. I’m not trying to make a big thing of it. It just feels very real to me.
Even when people you trust, like family or professionals, tell you there's no sign of anyone watching you or hearing a voice, do you still believe it's happening without any doubt?

I mean… I don’t want to say “without any doubt,” because I know that sounds stubborn. But yes, even when people I trust tell me they don’t see anything, I still feel like it’s really happening.

That’s part of why I’m here, I guess. People keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes. It feels like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband. I’m not trying to be difficult… it just feels true to me.
How long have you been feeling certain that the hospital people and the agency have been watching you, even when others have told you there’s no sign of it?

It’s been… I guess about 11 months now. Not quite a year, but close.

The voices and that feeling that people are watching us—watching me—have been going on that long. I know that sounds like a long time. I probably should’ve said something sooner, but I kept hoping maybe it would settle down or I could just handle it.
Even when you’ve been shown or told there’s no one at the window or no sign of anyone watching, do you still feel completely certain that they’re there, like it’s just a fact to you?

Yes… I do. I know people keep telling me there’s no one there, and I’m trying to be reasonable about it, I really am.

But it still feels like a fact to me that the hospital people and some people from the agency are watching the house and my cleaning routes. Like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.

I know that may not be the answer you want, but that’s how it feels to me.
Even when you’ve been shown or told there’s no one at the window or no sign of anyone watching, do you still feel completely certain that they’re there, like it’s just a fact to you?

Yes… I still feel certain. I know that probably sounds like I’m not listening, and I don’t mean to be difficult.

It’s just… when people say there’s no one there, I understand what they’re telling me, but it doesn’t change what I know. I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I really do believe the hospital people and some people from the agency have been watching our house, and even my cleaning routes, to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

I hope that makes sense… or at least, I’m trying to answer honestly.
Even when you’ve been shown or told there’s no one at the window or no sign of anyone watching, do you still feel completely certain that they’re there, like it’s just a fact to you?

I know I’ve said it already, and I don’t want to sound stubborn… but yes. Even when people tell me there’s no one there, it still feels true to me.

I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes. I think they’re checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. I’m trying to answer the way you’re asking, honestly.
